Yamaha NMAX Scooters Are Going Electric, 65-Mile Range Is on the Table with the E
45 photos
Photo: Yamaha
The scooter market is very profitable for those in this line of work these days, and that is pretty obvious just by looking at how many of them there are out there. Some are better at the job than others, but if you ask me, at least over in Europe, one scooter-making company reigns supreme: Yamaha.
The Japanese company has plenty of models on the table in this segment, but they still don't seem to be enough to satisfy people's appetite for Yamaha scooters. Especially when talking about the ones in the Max family, a go-to choice for many buyers over the past two and a half decades.
The range is a pretty solid one already, but up until this week, the week of the 2026 Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA), it didn't offer any version powered by an electric drivetrain. Well, now it does.
Enter the Yamaha NMAX E Sport Scooter, a newcomer to the range built on a brand-new platform tailored for an electric powertrain and designed to help the bike maker fulfill its commitment to a green future.
In more ways than one, the new two-wheeler is the same as the others in the range, but it opens up an entirely new segment for the company, one that could prove very lucrative in the troubled days we live through.
The NMAX E plays in the 125cc class, but it does so with a 3,5 kWh lithium-ion battery and a ten horsepower/ 33 Nm of torque clutchless permanent magnet synchronous motor that can spin at a maximum of 3,500 rpm.
The hardware has been designed to offer a maximum range of 64 miles (104 km), which is more than enough for daily commutes in crowded cities. Charging, though, could prove a bit of a challenge, as the small battery pack needs up to 5.5 hours to get from zero to 100 percent using the onboard 800W charger.
All of the fittings customers make use of on all the other Max scooters can be found on the E as well, including the three ride modes and the reverse function, the five-inch TFT display with smartphone connectivity, and the long dual seat.
Yamaha will roll out the new scooter model in the spring of next year, but, at least for now, it doesn't offer any info on price. We do know the two-wheeler will premiere two new color schemes, Avio Blue and Platinum Silver.
Taking advantage of the launch of the electric scooter, Yamaha has also birthed something called the YOU Charge, which it describes as a solution for quick and convenient access to public charging. The details on that are quite scarce at the moment, but we'll get back to that as soon as we know more.
